chapter: Early drum sets and dance-hall era
title: Big-band drummers and Sonny South
summary: He names big-band drummers Sidney Montague and Stanley, the Sonny South orchestra, and his neighbor Professor Shalla Neal.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Well I do know Sidney Montague, the drummer, and let's see who else. Stanley, well those guys was playing in the big bands. What are you used to do with that big band? Now this guy, Alfred Martin, I think he used to name.
What he used to have, that was the guy that played in the big orchestra. Yeah, it was this year ago.
Who's Stanley? Stanley, what's his name?

I don't know Stanley's name. All I know about Stanley, he's a wonderful drummer. Who did he play with? He played with Seventy Days, he played with Father Seles. Anything on the information now, we're playing right through.

Oh, let's see. I better put down here, this is real too of Chester Jones, July the 10th, 1961. You just mentioned Stanley and Sidney Montague, how they, you're talking about how they had a bigger set of drums or something?

Yeah, they used those big types. They didn't have the small set of drums out there. Sidney Montague, he used to play with the Sonny South, and he played with the Sonny, I mean with the Sidney Days Means Band. That's a number of bands he played with.

That was a big band around here too, one of those big officers they had around here. A fellow by the name of MacNeil, I think was the leader of that band, he's a trumpet player. MacNeil. Yeah. I don't know his first name, but I know or remember MacNeil. I remember when he was taking lessons from the old fellow by the name of Shala Neal, he was a professor. Shala Neal standing right around the corner from my house and I used to go around there and play with his grandson and I was always friends. We went to school together. Used to be at his house a lot. Well now, that's the only time I ever had a chance to play on the drum when I used to go to East out here. All he had was a little snare drum, but he first used to try to teach him. Most of the time he was out in the backyard playing and we'd have the drum out there playing. Another fellow I know that Professor Tuck, he went great for a good while and a number of years. I don't know if he's still playing or not. Albert Schneier, you ever heard of him?
